 on
 CMA 8 agenda item 4
Matters relating to the global stocktake: report on the annual global stocktake dialogue
 referred to in paragraph 187 of decision 1/CMA.5
 Version 16/11/2026 14:00
 The Conference of the Parties serving as the meeting of the Parties to the Paris
 Agreement,
 Recalling Article 14 of the Paris Agreement,
 Also recalling decisions 1/CMA.5 and 3/CMA.7,

1. Expresses appreciation to the Chairs of the Subsidiary Body for Scientific and
 Technological Advice and the Subsidiary Body for Implementation, as well as the secretariat,
 for convening in 2026 the third annual dialogue [, as referred to in paragraph 187 of decision
 1/CMA.5, ] on how the outcomes of the global stocktake are informing the preparation of
 nationally determined contributions, and for preparing the summary report thereon1 and
 expresses gratitude to Parties, and observers and other non-Party stakeholders for
 contributing to the discussions at the dialogue;

2. [Notes with appreciation][Welcomes] the summary report on the third annual global
 stocktake dialogue;

3. Encourages Parties to draw on the lessons learned and good practices from the
 summary report[s] on the [first, second and] third annual global stocktake dialogue[s], as
 appreciate, in their national contexts and processes; 4. Option 1: no text
 Option 2: [Placeholder for broad context: the following elements are presented for
 individual consideration]
 • Acknowledges Parties’ efforts in preparing and implementing their latest nationally
 determined contributions, including efforts to be informed by the outcomes of the first
 global stocktake[, including paragraph 39, 40 and 171 of decision 1/CMA.5,][and
 encourages Parties that have not yet communicated nationally determined contributions
 in the latest round thereof to do so as soon as possible];

• Acknowledges the capacity constraints of developing country Parties and that challenges,
 gaps and barriers remain with regard to preparing and implementing nationally
 determined contributions, [recognizing the special circumstances of the least developed
 countries and small island developing States,][noting [the need for][the importance of]
 [more predictable, accessible [and grant-based] financial support [from developed
 country Parties] [from a wide variety of sources], as well as capacity-building and
 technology development and transfer, to enable developing country Parties to develop
 and implement their nationally determined contributions;]
 • Recognizes gaps in ambition, implementation and support and the need to enhance
 [ambition,] implementation, support [for developing country Parties] and international
 cooperation in pursuing efforts [to limit global temperature increase to 1.5 °C and to
 limit both the magnitude and duration of any temperature overshoot][to achieve the long-
 term goals of the Paris Agreement and the objective of the Convention];

• [Recognizes the importance of supportive, open and just international economic and
 trade cooperation for the effective implementation of nationally determined
 contributions and expresses serious concern that unilateral trade-related measures
 1 FCCC/PA/CMA/2026/3. constitute barriers to such implementation, including through their adverse impacts on
 competitiveness and market access;]
 • [Highlights that the 1.5 °C pathways set out in the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report as
 referred to in the outcomes of the first global stocktake, informed nationally determined
 efforts, including when setting intermediate and long-term targets, including for 2035;]
 5. Option 1: Encourages Parties to take into account the information and views reflected
 in the summary reports on the [first, 2 second 3] and third annual global stocktake
 dialogues, [as appropriate][, in discussions under the second global stocktake]; Option 2: no text

6. Acknowledges that those dialogues facilitated the sharing of knowledge and
 perspectives [by Parties, and observers and other non-Party stakeholders][, including
 Indigenous Peoples,] on how the outcomes of the global stocktake are informing the
 preparation of nationally determined contributions[, highlights the value of the annual global
 stocktake dialogue as a space for sharing experience and lessons learned relevant to the
 preparation and implementation of nationally determined contributions] [and reaffirms that
 it will consider the resumption of the annual global stocktake dialogue, which concluded at
 the sixty-fourth sessions of the subsidiary bodies, in the context of its consideration of the
 outcome of the second global stocktake4][and recalls decision 3/CMA.7 paragraph 14].

7. [Recognizes the value of peer-to-peer exchanges in supporting the preparation and
 implementation of nationally determined contributions, welcomes the efforts of the
 secretariat, including through its regional collaboration centres, in collaboration with relevant
 partners, to facilitate knowledge-sharing and mutual learning among Parties, and encourages
 continued collaboration to strengthen such exchanges and support countries in their NDC
 preparation and implementation.]
2 FCCC/PA/CMA/2024/5.
3 FCCC/PA/CMA/2025/6.
4 Decision 3/CMA.7, para. 14.

 on
 CMA 8 agenda item 4
Matters relating to the global stocktake: report on the annual global stocktake dialogue
 referred to in paragraph 187 of decision 1/CMA.5
 Version 19/11/2026 7:30
 The Conference of the Parties serving as the meeting of the Parties to the Paris
 Agreement,
 Recalling Article 14 of the Paris Agreement,
 Also recalling decisions 1/CMA.5 and 3/CMA.7,

1. Expresses appreciation to the Chairs of the Subsidiary Body for Scientific and
 Technological Advice and the Subsidiary Body for Implementation, as well as the secretariat,
 for convening in 2026 the third annual dialogue, as referred to in paragraph 187 of decision
 1/CMA.5, on how the outcomes of the global stocktake are informing the preparation of
 nationally determined contributions, and for preparing the summary report thereon1 and
 expresses gratitude to Parties, and observers and other non-Party stakeholders for
 contributing to the discussions at the dialogue;

2. Notes with appreciation the summary report on the third annual global stocktake
 dialogue;

5. Encourages Parties that have not yet communicated nationally determined
 contributions in the latest round thereof to do so as soon as possible;

6. Recognizes the capacity constraints of developing country Parties and that challenges,
 gaps and barriers remain with regard to preparing nationally determined contributions, and
 reaffirms the importance of financial, technology development and transfer, and capacity-
 building support, as well as international cooperation, to help enable developing country
 Parties to develop their nationally determined contributions;

7. Acknowledges that those dialogues facilitated the sharing of knowledge and
 perspectives by Parties, observers and all other non-Party stakeholders on how the outcomes
 of the global stocktake are informing the preparation of nationally determined contributions,
 highlights the value of the annual global stocktake dialogue as a space for sharing experience
 and lessons learned relevant to the preparation of nationally determined contributions and
 recalls that it will consider the resumption of the annual global stocktake dialogue, which
 concluded at the sixty-fourth sessions of the subsidiary bodies, in the context of its
 consideration of the outcome of the second global stocktake, as per decision 3/CMA.7,
 paragraph 14.

8. Recognizes the value of exchanges among Parties in supporting the preparation and
 implementation of nationally determined contributions, welcomes the efforts of the
 secretariat, including through its regional collaboration centres, in collaboration with relevant
 partners, to facilitate knowledge-sharing and mutual learning among Parties, and encourages
 such collaboration.
 1 FCCC/PA/CMA/2026/3.
